stories.headline: US Commerce awards $2B to nine quantum firms and takes equity stakes; IBM gets $1B

key_facts.fact: The US Department of Commerce signed letters of intent on May 21 to provide $2.013 billion in CHIPS and Science Act incentives to nine quantum companies.
key_facts.excerpt: The Department of Commerce today announced the signing of 9 letters of intent to provide $2.013 billion in federal incentives under the CHIPS and Science Act.

key_facts.fact: Funding goes to two 'quantum foundry' companies, GlobalFoundries ($375M) and IBM ($1B), plus seven quantum computing firms: Atom Computing, Diraq, D-Wave, Infleqtion, PsiQuantum, Quantinuum and Rigetti.
key_facts.excerpt: The most substantial funding is slated for the two foundry companies, with $375 million for Global Foundries and $1 billion for IBM. The other companies received between $38 and $100 million each.

key_facts.fact: D-Wave, Rigetti and Infleqtion will each get about $100 million, while Diraq will receive up to $38 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Other firms including D-Wave, Rigetti Computing and Infleqtion will get about $100 million each, while Diraq will receive up to $38 million.

key_facts.fact: The Department of Commerce will receive a minority, non-controlling equity stake in each company as a condition for the funds, to 'enhance the return for the U.S. taxpayer.'
key_facts.excerpt: The Department will receive a minority, non-controlling equity stake in each company as a condition for receiving the funds to enhance the return for the U.S. taxpayer.

key_facts.fact: IBM's $1 billion will fund a new standalone company called Anderon, based in New Albany, New York, billed as America's first dedicated quantum chip manufacturing facility.
key_facts.excerpt: IBM announced the CHIPS incentive would support research-and-development efforts of a new company called Anderon. That standalone IBM company 'will operate as a state-of-the-art 300-millimeter quantum wafer foundry.'

key_facts.fact: The Trump administration framed the move as a push to secure US leadership in quantum and counter China.
key_facts.excerpt: The Trump administration will take $2 billion in equity stakes across nine quantum-computing companies, including a new IBM venture, in a major push to secure U.S. leadership in the emerging technology and counter China.

stories.headline: Newsom signs first-of-its-kind order to shield California workers from AI displacement

key_facts.fact: California Gov. Gavin Newsom signed a 'first-of-its-kind' executive order on May 21 directing state agencies to prepare workers and businesses for AI-driven workforce disruption.
key_facts.excerpt: Gov. Gavin Newsom issued on Thursday what his office called a 'first-of-its-kind' executive order directing state agencies to prepare workers and businesses for artificial intelligence-driven workforce disruption.

key_facts.fact: The order tells agencies to work with labor groups, academics and the AI industry to study subsidies for companies that retain workers instead of replacing them with AI.
key_facts.excerpt: [The order] orders state agencies to collaborate with labor groups, academics and the AI industry to look at possible subsidies for companies that retain workers instead of replacing them with autonomous machines.

key_facts.fact: Policy options to be studied include severance standards, expanded unemployment insurance, retraining for white-collar roles, worker-ownership models, a universal basic income study, and 'universal basic capital' giving residents stakes in stocks, bonds or wealth funds.
key_facts.excerpt: The order mandates agencies to explore a range of policy options, including severance standards, expanded unemployment insurance, job retraining programs aimed specifically at white-collar workers, worker ownership models and a concept the governor called 'universal basic capital,' giving all residents a stake in assets such as corporate stocks, bonds or wealth funds.

key_facts.fact: Newsom argued the status quo is untenable: 'you cannot continue to have a payroll tax system that taxes jobs and then subsidizes automation.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'Businesses are going to make a fortune, and that's why you cannot continue to have a payroll tax system that taxes jobs and then subsidizes automation,' Newsom said.

key_facts.fact: California is home to 33 of the world's top 50 private AI companies; the order requires a dashboard showing AI's impact across sectors and stronger tracking of hiring and payroll trends.
key_facts.excerpt: State agencies are tasked with creating a dashboard to display AI's impact across various sectors and drafting a report on potential labor disruptions within the tech-heavy state, which is home to 33 of the world's top 50 private AI companies.

key_facts.fact: The order prescribes no direct action yet and may clash with the Trump administration's hands-off stance and efforts to preempt state AI rules.
key_facts.excerpt: It may come into conflict with the federal government's current stance on AI, however. The Trump administration has broadly advocated for a hands-off approach to the AI industry and has sought to preempt state regulations.

stories.headline: Trump postpones AI security order signing, says it 'could have been a blocker'

key_facts.fact: The White House abruptly postponed the Thursday afternoon (May 21) ceremony for Trump to sign an executive order on AI and cybersecurity, hours before it was due.
key_facts.excerpt: The White House postponed a highly anticipated signing of an artificial intelligence executive order, according to four people with knowledge of the matter.

key_facts.fact: Trump said he postponed it because 'I didn't like certain aspects of it... we're leading China, we're leading everybody, and I don't want to do anything that's going to get in the way of that lead,' calling it a potential 'blocker.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'Because I didn't like certain aspects of it, I postponed it,' Mr. Trump said. 'I think it gets in the way of, you know, we're leading China, we're leading everybody, and I don't want to do anything that's going to get in the way of that lead.'

key_facts.fact: The order would have established a voluntary framework giving the federal government pre-release access to 'covered frontier models', with a proposed 90-day review window that some industry leaders wanted cut to 14 days.
key_facts.excerpt: One of the key sticking points in the EO's language, per CNN, is a proposed requirement for AI companies to share advanced models with the government between 14 and 90 days ahead of launch.

key_facts.fact: It would also have directed agencies to use advanced AI to strengthen cybersecurity for federal, state and local systems and critical sectors like banks and hospitals.
key_facts.excerpt: The executive order was intended to help protect US computer systems from powerful artificial intelligence that could give bad actors unprecedented powers.

key_facts.fact: Reports cite a more mundane reason: several tech CEOs invited to the photo op could not reach Washington on short notice, with some reportedly midair when the event was called off.
key_facts.excerpt: The unofficial reason: Not enough tech CEOs could make it to Washington, D.C. on short notice, according to several reports. And what's an executive order signing without a photo op?

key_facts.fact: The effort grew from cyber-risk fears tied to powerful models like Anthropic's Mythos and OpenAI's GPT-5.5 Cyber, which can quickly find and exploit security vulnerabilities.
key_facts.excerpt: This is partly in response to concerns from the release of Anthropic's Mythos and OpenAI's GPT-5.5 Cyber, both of which can quickly find and exploit security vulnerabilities.

stories.headline: Oil jumps ~3% as Iran uranium directive and Hormuz toll dispute stall peace talks

key_facts.fact: Oil rose about 3% on Thursday May 21: US WTI crude climbed 3.6% to $101.78 and Brent rose 2.9% to $108.09 a barrel.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude futures gained $3.07, or 2.9%, to $108.09 a barrel at 11:12 a.m. EDT. U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures rose $3.52, or 3.6%, to $101.78.

key_facts.fact: Prices spiked after a Reuters report that Iran's Supreme Leader directed that the country's near-weapons-grade uranium not be sent abroad, denting hopes for a quick end to the war.
key_facts.excerpt: Crude prices jumped today after Reuters reported that Iran's Supreme Leader said enriched uranium must stay in Iran, as sending the material abroad would leave the country more vulnerable to future attacks.

key_facts.fact: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said a proposed Iranian tolling system in the Strait of Hormuz would make a diplomatic deal 'unfeasible': 'No one is in favor of a tolling system.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'No one is in favor of a tolling system, it can't happen, it would be unacceptable and it would make a diplomatic deal unfeasible.'

key_facts.fact: Trump said he wants the strait 'free; we don't want tolls' and warned he is ready to resume strikes if he doesn't get the 'right answers' from Tehran.
key_facts.excerpt: Trump has said he is ready to resume strikes on Iran, which the U.S. and ally Israel first launched in late February, if he does not get the 'right answers' from Iran's leadership.

key_facts.fact: Iran said the latest US proposal 'reduced the gaps to some extent' as Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir traveled to Tehran to mediate; uranium enrichment and Hormuz control remain the main sticking points.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran said the latest US proposal 'reduced the gaps to some extent' as powerful Pakistani army chief Asim Munir traveled to Tehran... a senior Iranian official [said] that Iran's uranium enrichment and its control over the Strait of Hormuz remain among the sticking points.

key_facts.fact: The Strait of Hormuz carried about 20% of the world's oil and LNG before the war, with 125-140 daily passages now reduced to a trickle; the IEA warns the market could enter a 'red zone' in July-August.
key_facts.excerpt: Some ships are managing to transit the strait, but only a trickle compared with the 125-140 daily passages before the war... It warned that the peak of summer fuel demand coupled [with limited supply means the market could enter the 'red zone'] in July and August.

stories.headline: WSJ: Iranian network moved about $850M through Binance to fund the IRGC

key_facts.fact: A network linked to Iranian businessman Babak Zanjani, a self-described 'antisanction' operator, moved roughly $850 million in crypto through Binance accounts over about two years, per internal Binance compliance reports cited by the WSJ.
key_facts.excerpt: Babak Zanjani, an Iranian businessman and self-described 'antisanction' operator, reportedly conducted about $850 million in transactions over two years on the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, according to internal Binance compliance reports cited by The Wall Street Journal.

key_facts.fact: The funds reportedly moved through Binance-linked channels to networks financing Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), per Binance compliance reports, blockchain data, foreign law-enforcement officials and nonpublic documents.
key_facts.excerpt: The funds form part of broader crypto transactions that reportedly moved through Binance-linked channels to networks financing Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps in the years preceding the current US-Iran conflict.

key_facts.fact: Terrorism-financing experts estimate roughly half the $850 million may have moved through networks tied to Iran's military structure.
key_facts.excerpt: The $850 million in Zanjani-linked activity, including deposits and withdrawals, could indicate that roughly half the amount moved through networks tied to financing operations linked to Iran's military structure.

key_facts.fact: One main account allegedly remained active for at least 15 months and was still operating as of January 2026 despite internal alerts about suspicious transactions.
key_facts.excerpt: One main account allegedly remained active for at least 15 months and was still operational as of January 2026, despite internal alerts about suspicious transactions.

key_facts.fact: Iran's central bank reportedly transferred $107 million in cryptocurrency into Binance accounts last year, according to blockchain analysis.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's central bank reportedly transferred $107 million in cryptocurrency through a series of transactions into Binance accounts last year, according to blockchain analysis.

key_facts.fact: Binance rejected the allegations, saying it does not allow transactions involving sanctioned individuals and has significantly strengthened its compliance and anti-money-laundering systems.
key_facts.excerpt: Binance rejected the allegations, stating that it does not allow transactions involving sanctioned individuals and that it has significantly strengthened its compliance and anti-money laundering systems in recent years.

stories.headline: FDA approves AstraZeneca's Baxfendy, a first-in-class drug for uncontrolled hypertension

key_facts.fact: The US FDA approved AstraZeneca's Baxfendy (baxdrostat), a first-in-class aldosterone synthase inhibitor, to treat hypertension in combination with other antihypertensives in adults whose blood pressure is not adequately controlled.
key_facts.excerpt: AstraZeneca's Baxfendy (baxdrostat) has been approved by the US FDA as a first-in-class aldosterone synthase inhibitor (ASI) to treat hypertension in combination with other antihypertensive medications, to lower blood pressure in adults who are not adequately controlled.

key_facts.fact: Approval was based on the Phase 3 BaxHTN trial, which showed statistically significant systolic blood pressure reductions at both 2mg and 1mg doses in patients with uncontrolled and resistant hypertension already on two or more medications.
key_facts.excerpt: The approval was based on positive results from the BaxHTN phase 3 trial, with Baxfendy demonstrating statistically significant and clinically meaningful seated systolic blood pressure reduction at both 2mg and 1mg doses in patients with uncontrolled and resistant hypertension on two or more medications.

key_facts.fact: Baxfendy was generally well-tolerated with no unanticipated safety findings; hypertension affects more than 1.4 billion people worldwide, many uncontrolled despite multiple therapies.
key_facts.excerpt: Baxfendy was generally well-tolerated with no unanticipated safety findings. Hypertension affects more than 1.4 billion people worldwide and many patients remain uncontrolled despite multiple therapies.

stories.headline: EU to propose lifting China chip sanctions weeks after imposing them, to shield automakers

key_facts.fact: The European Commission will propose temporarily lifting sanctions on Chinese semiconductor supplier Yangzhou Yangjie Electronic Technology, possibly as early as this week.
key_facts.excerpt: The European Commission, the EU's executive arm, will propose the exemption for chip manufacturer Yangzhou Yangjie Electronic Technology as early as this week, according to people familiar with the matter.

key_facts.fact: Yangjie was added in April to the EU's 20th sanctions package targeting entities accused of supplying dual-use goods or weapons systems to Russia, with its products allegedly found in drones and glide bombs used against Ukraine.
key_facts.excerpt: Yangjie Electronic was included in the EU's 20th sanctions package... The Chinese semiconductor firm was sanctioned in April after dozens of shipments of its technologies allegedly reached Russia and its products were found in drones and glide bombs used against Ukraine.

key_facts.fact: European automakers lobbied to delay the ban, warning that chip inventories would be depleted within weeks and force production stoppages across the continent.
key_facts.excerpt: European automakers warned that without the derogation, chip inventories would be exhausted within weeks, forcing production stoppages across the continent.

key_facts.fact: Any derogation would be temporary, lasting several months to give industry time to find alternative suppliers, and would require approval from all 27 EU member states.
key_facts.excerpt: Any derogation would be temporary and likely last several months to give the industry more time to find alternative suppliers.

key_facts.fact: The move follows the Nexperia crisis, in which the Dutch government seized control of the chipmaker from Chinese parent Wingtech and Beijing retaliated with export controls, forcing temporary shutdowns at Honda, Volkswagen and Bosch.
key_facts.excerpt: Yangjie had become a crutch for sourcing components after the Dutch government seized control of Nexperia from its Chinese parent Wingtech last October. Beijing retaliated with export controls on the chipmaker's Chinese-made output, forcing temporary production shutdowns at Honda, Volkswagen, Bosch, and others.
